newsitem.title: UK: UK's DSF Furniture to open further 15-20 stores.
newsitem.headline: UK's DSF Furniture to open further 15-20 stores.

text.p: British retailer DFS Furniture Co Plc said on Tuesday it planned to open a further 15 to 20 new stores over three years as it continue the expansion of the group it initiated in earnest in 1995.

"We're about 2-1/2 years into the three years we gave ourselves to open 15 to 20 stores. We're going to do that quite easily....(and) expansion in the next three years will be at a similar level," said chairman Sir Graham Kirkham in a telephone interview.
DFS opened eight stores in 1995/96 -- including its first in London -- and two more in the first half of the current year. It has opened three more since.
The specialist retailer and manufacturer of upholstered furniture will open three more stores by the end of 1997, said chief operating officer Jon Massey.
Kirkham said the company remains a strong cash generator and expects to fund expansion from its own cash resources.

The group reported a 23.6 percent jump in pre-tax profits to 18.7 million pounds ($30.5 million) -- above an expected figure of 18 million -- for the six months to January 25. Sales surged 43.9 percent to 126.3 million pounds.
DFS shares, recently depressed after rival MFI Furniture Group Plc in March posted a surprise slowdown in sales growth, rose 12-1/2 pence to 545 on the London Stock Exchange.
"There is a sense of relief," said one trader.
MFI had warned in March that its market had yet to see a sustained pickup in demand.

"Whatever happens (at MFI) there's an assumption it will happen here, and nothing could be further from the truth," said Kirkham. Both are found under the furniture banner, but DFS is a specialist selling primarily one product while MFI sells a wider range to a different sector of the market, he added.
"We've never expected....to be a beneficiary of (factors like) housing booms or look to get a benefit from trading in a buoyant economy. We've tended to win market share," he said.
Current trading was similar to the first half, he added.
"I am confident and optimistic about the long term and look forward to reporting continuing growth and success at the full year," Kirkham said in a statement accompanying the results.
DFS reported a 25.8 percent rise in the interim dividend to 3.9 pence. Earnings per share rose 23.5 percent to 11.84 pence. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
